To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the non-Abelian gauge symmetry in the six-dimensional F (4) theory arises from a massive type IIA background with a nontrivial warp factor and a non-vanishing dilaton.
the Romans F (3) gauged theory in five dimensions is a consistent reduction of the massive type IIA theory on a S 3.
the Romans F ( 4 ) gauged supergravities in six dimensions are the consistent warped S 3 reductions of massive IIA supergravity.

a systematic study of the structure of supersymmetric field theories in various dimensions, with particular emphasis on the study of supersymmetry breaking and the construction of supersymmetric models of particle physics.

the study of the non-linear Kalu-Klein ansätze for the reduction of massive type IIB supergravity and type IIA supergravities with a non-zero Romans mass to six and five-dimensional supergravities, respectively.

the Romans F ( 4 ) gauged supergravities in six dimensions, as the low-energy effective theories of the massive type II superstrings, are described by a set of 3D gauged supercoset sigma-models with an appropriate gauging.
there is a consistent warped S4 reduction of the bosons of massive IIA supergravity, which yields the Romans gauged F(4) supergravity.

there is no evidence of any significant effect of the 2D and 3D effects on the 4D and 5D results, and therefore no reason to expect any significant effect of 4D and/or 5D effects on the observed 2D and/or 3D effects.
